newsitem.title: FRANCE: Suspected Turkish guerrilla leader held in France.
newsitem.headline: Suspected Turkish guerrilla leader held in France.

text.p: A suspected leader of Turkey's extreme left Dev Sol guerrilla group has been detained in France and put under investigation on suspicion of activities linked to terrorism, justice sources said on Tuesday.
Mehmet Akdemir, 34, was detained on Friday at the Franco-Swiss border and a French magistrate specialising in terrorism cases formally opened a probe into him late on Monday, the sources said.
Akdemir was placed under investigation on suspicion of criminal collusion and using falsified official documents in the framework of what was described as "a terrorist enterprise."
Justice sources said Akdemir was arrested after Swiss officials barred him from entering Switzerland when they found his identity documents were fake.

The sources said Dev Sol was held responsible for several violent actions outside Turkey since its creation in 1978, including murders, and was believed to finance itself through extorting money from Turks abroad.
Eleven Dev Sol militants were sentenced to prison terms of up to four years by a Paris court earlier this month.
